name: arrival
description: Open model -- applies load by **arrival rate**, regardless of whether the previous request has returned. This is something JMeter's default Thread Group cannot do (requires the jpgc Arrivals Thread Group plugin).
_why: OREO's load is naturally an arrival rate: ~120 trades/day submitted independently by traders, and **nobody waits for the previous trade to finish before submitting the next**. A closed model brakes itself when the server degrades, masking the consequences of overload; an open model lets queues genuinely pile up.
_derivation: Production is ~120 trades/day. To gather enough samples in an acceptable duration, time must be compressed: rate=1/s is hundreds of times the production peak, used to find 'at what arrival rate queuing begins'. For the actual sweep run one round each with -e RATE=1 / 2 / 4 / 8.
_preAllocatedVUs: VUs needed ~= rate x time-per-iteration. rate=1 at 3s per iteration -> 3. Pre-allocating 20 leaves headroom for degradation; if insufficient, k6 grows toward maxVUs and warns in the summary (which is itself a signal: the system cannot keep up with the arrival rate).

thresholds._dropped: dropped_iterations > 0 means maxVUs was insufficient and the arrival rate was not fully applied -- results are unusable
thresholds._circuitBreaker: Two-tier design: the strict rate>0.99 line is the end-of-run VERDICT; the loose rate>0.50 line with abortOnFail is a CIRCUIT BREAKER that only kills clearly doomed runs (wholesale business rejection = stale data, whether stale at launch or gone stale mid-run). Loose on purpose: at low throughput a couple of legitimate transient failures must not abort a long run. delayAbortEval lets the sample size build up first. This replaces the removed setup() probe request, covering the whole run instead of one instant before it.
